quarterly_data.signal: CALL (verbatim) — Q2 DETAIL AND OUTLOOK MECHANICS, CFO Chantelle Breithaupt: Q2 revenue just over $3 billion, above the $2.8 billion guide, growth 'driven by our AI and enterprise customers'. International revenues $697.8 million, 23% of total revenue, up from 13.5% last quarter (organic international growth plus a shift in the geographic mix of sales to large global customers). Gross margin 63.4%, up from 62.4% in the prior quarter on tariff refunds and customer mix — 'probably 20-30 basis points of tariff refund' versus guide, and 'I wouldn't put anything in there yet due to a price increase'. Operating expenses $411 million (13.5% of revenue), up on 'additional investment in liquid cooling, high Radix switching, and AI optimizing software'; R&D $278.1 million (9.2% of revenue). Cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities approximately $13.3 billion; cash from operations approximately $1.1 billion; inventory $2.5 billion (from $2.4 billion), turns 1.7; capex $29.7 million, with the expanded Santa Clara facilities expected complete by the end of fiscal 2026. FY2026 gross-margin range 62%-64% includes 'anticipated supply chain cost increases for memory and silicon'; tax rate approximately 21.5%. Customer visibility: 'we still have the same kind of two quarters of visibility'.
quarterly_data.figure: International $697.8M (23% of revenue, from 13.5%); opex $411M; R&D $278.1M; cash ~$13.3B; inventory $2.5B; two quarters of visibility

quarterly_data.signal: CALL (verbatim) — SUPPLY STATUS: COO Todd Nightingale: 'We've secured multi-year agreements with leading vendors of strategic components, qualified new suppliers in key areas to limit risk, and built out supply chains for next-gen AI technologies'; 'Relationships with our strategic silicon vendors continue to be strong, with really excellent collaboration in both supply chain and technical engagements'; better delivery terms mean 'shorter lead times and being more nimble' — 'If our demand shifts from one SKU to another, we're carrying less risk'; improved lead times and inventory management 'of thousands of component SKUs'. CEO Jayshree Ullal: 'While the industry-wide supply tightness and rising component costs persist, Arista has taken individual and aggressive proactive steps'; 'We are also partnering closely with our key suppliers to meet our prioritized forecasts'; 'I don't want you to believe that suddenly we waved a magic wand and all our problems have gone away.' CFO: the $9.7 billion of purchase commitments 'mostly represents purchases for chips related to new products and AI deployments'; inventory fluctuations are expected to continue while balancing component timing and availability.
quarterly_data.figure: Purchase commitments $9.7B, mostly chips for new products and AI deployments

quarterly_data.signal: CALL (verbatim) — EOS VERSUS WHITE BOX AND THE MULTI-MODEL VIEW: CEO Jayshree Ullal: 'white box is certainly a tactical solution that we tend to see more in use cases that are simple scale up or scale out, where the actual amount of software and system requirements are low'; customers choose the 7800 AI spine 'to achieve that high scale without adding additional tiers'; 'more and more customers want either EOS itself in its entirety or a hybrid combination, often of OpenNOS and EOS'; 'Most of these neo clouds don't have staff'; 'in this current scarcity of supply chain and people and needing to deploy AI fast, Arista's really winning out with the system-wide approach on EOS and good hardware.' Some customers 'will just prefer to go with the white box because it's ultra-cheap, or that have large amounts of staff like the Titans often do'. CTO Ken Duda: 'The more diversity there is among models and model makers and between AI infrastructure providers, the better for us'; MRC and UEC work are examples of 'open, interoperable standards'.

CALL (verbatim) — WHERE THE RAISE COMES FROM: CEO Jayshree Ullal on the AI and campus goals: 'If you had to ask me whether our AI number or campus number will go up, I think Chantelle, Todd, Ken, and I absolutely believe it will. The question is not whether it will go up. The question is what is that number?' — 'we can most certainly say all numbers are going up.' The $1.1 billion raise is expected 'to consist of all our product sectors', including enterprise and routing (edge routing, DCI and scale-across); the core front-end data center 'isn't going to be flat'. CFO: growth drivers outside AI include 'the new logo acquisition', international growth and 'land and expand' from campus to data center and back.
